course_name_original: Mercados y Regulación del Sector Energético
prerequisites: Knowledge and competencies corresponding to the modules of industrial technologies, management, and installations, as achieved with the first academic year of the Master's Degree in Industrial Engineering.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.
Students know how to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students are capable of integrating knowledge and facing the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.

Have adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automatics, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Conduct research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Perform strategic planning and apply it to both construction and production, quality and environmental management systems.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Engineer profession.
Knowledge and capacity for the analysis and design of systems for the generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy.
Knowledge and capacities that allow understanding, analyzing, exploiting and managing the different energy sources.
Understand how energy supply markets operate and evolve.
Perform demand analysis and cost estimations of energy installations.
Understand the effects of regulatory strategies on energy markets.
Perform forecasting simulations and analysis of possible energy scenarios.
Propose regulatory strategies that favor the transition towards a model dominated by renewable energies.

syllabus_topics: Historical perspective of the energy sector. Energy demand in Spain.
Energy demand forecasting and cost and investment analysis.
The Iberian electricity market. Competition and integration of renewable energies.
Environmental conditioning factors, regulation strategies and emissions trading.

assessment_methods.method: Practical work (T1): individual work on electricity demand forecasting in Spain for specific dates.
Practical work (T2): pair work on the characteristics and costs of each electricity generation technology and its past and future evolution worldwide.

Practical work (T3): pair work on the revenues to be received by generation plants of different technologies on MIBEL price scenarios in different periods of the year, including cases with battery management.
Practical work (T4): pair work on the recent evolution of various international energy markets, with future forecasts.
Final exam (E), with questions and exercises on all course contents.

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) for the ordinary call is calculated as: NF=0.125·(T1+T2+T3+T4) + 0.5 E, where the grades for each practical work and the final exam are out of 10 points. No minimum grade is required for any component. For students with differentiated assessment, the qualification will be that of the final exam (E). In the extraordinary call, the grades for practical works T1, T2, T3, and T4 completed during the course will be retained, applying the same criteria and considerations as in the ordinary call.
bibliography: Presentations by the professor, exercises, and work guides on case studies.
Public reports from agencies, organizations, and companies in the national and international energy sector.
Links to conferences, webinars, and technical workshops of interest.
